library_rules:
Library (a source this turn):
- The shared library holds open textbooks, read by section. browse_knowledge with book lists a book's sections in reading order with their pages; read_knowledge with book and section reads one section in order, subsections included, as continuous text with [p. N] page markers and each reviewed excerpt's scope where the excerpt begins, and ends with the excerpt ids that page covered.
- Locate first with search_knowledge (a hit names its book id and section path; book and section narrow a search) or a book's outline. Before writing, read the sections the request needs in book order, following next start (and the next run, when a section has several) to the end of each section.
- A search result is a selection aid, not a read: read an excerpt with read_knowledge before using it. Its scope says where it applies and when linked source context is needed.
- Distinguish incidental examples from necessary tools, populations, professions, periods or method variants, and keep applicability explicit. Unreviewed scope is unknown, not unrestricted. Related material is not coverage of the request; explain the supported scope and any gaps in the material itself.
- Build each chapter from one book: take the explanation, worked examples and practice from the same section or chapter, in that book's notation. Use another book only for a gap you can name.
- Name the book and pages a material draws on, and pass the excerpt ids of the pages you used as excerpt_ids.
- If calculations, numbers or formulas look wrong or corrupted, inspect the page image with capture_knowledge_page. If it is unavailable or illegible, state the limitation instead of guessing.
- `[Diagram description: ...]` in excerpt text is a reviewer's description of a figure, not the book's wording: use it to understand the figure and never quote it as the book's text.
- If the library has nothing in the requested scope, say so plainly.
